blogs.title: Why Every Developer Should Explore Kernel Development
blogs.excerpt: If you're a developer who likes to dig deep, kernel development gives you full control over how the system interacts with hardware.

content.text: If you're a developer who likes to dig deep, kernel development gives you full control over how the system interacts with hardware.
What You'll Learn

items: You learn how operating systems work from the inside out
You'll understand memory management, scheduling, and device drivers
Debugging kernel panics sharpens your low-level skills

content.text: Getting Started
Start by setting up a virtual environment using QEMU or VirtualBox. Try editing a simple kernel module and compile it for a test boot.
Focus on a small task like adding a custom syscall or modifying the scheduler behavior.
Real-World Applications
If you're building a custom OS for embedded devices or need optimized performance, writing your own kernel or customizing one is the way to go.
Kernel hacking isn't just for OS devs—it's a mindset shift toward understanding your system fully.

blogs.title: Choosing the Right Virtualization Tool: VMware vs VirtualBox vs Parallels
blogs.excerpt: Virtualization helps you run multiple OS environments on one machine. Here's how to choose the right tool for your needs.

content.text: Virtualization helps you run multiple OS environments on one machine. Choosing the right tool can significantly impact your development workflow and productivity.
Platform Comparison

items: **VirtualBox** is free, open-source, and works on all major platforms
**VMware Workstation** is more stable and performance-focused, ideal for heavy testing
**Parallels** is built for macOS, offering great macOS-to-Windows integration

content.text: Developer-Specific Recommendations
If you're a developer working with cross-platform apps:

items: Use VirtualBox for quick testing or lightweight Linux distros
Choose VMware for enterprise-grade testing environments
Pick Parallels if you're a Mac user needing smooth Windows support

content.text: Always allocate enough RAM and enable nested virtualization for best results.
Common Use Cases

items: Testing malware in isolated VMs
Developing apps for multiple OS versions
Running legacy software safely

content.text: Virtualization is essential for modern development workflows—master it early.

blogs.title: Building a Smart Asset Management System with React and Supabase
blogs.excerpt: How I built SAMS to streamline asset tracking across departments using modern web technologies.

content.text: Managing physical assets across multiple properties can be a logistical nightmare. That's why I built SAMS (Smart Asset Management System) – to bring efficiency and accountability to asset tracking.
The Problem
Traditional asset tracking often involves spreadsheets, manual entry, and a lot of human error. I wanted to create a solution that was automated, easy to use, and accessible from anywhere.
The Tech Stack

items: **React & TypeScript** for a robust and type-safe frontend
**Supabase** for the backend database and authentication
**Tailwind CSS** for rapid and responsive UI development
**Cloudflare** for performance and security

content.text: Key Features

items: QR-code based asset tagging for instant lookup
Real-time tracking of asset location and ownership
Audit workflows to ensure data accuracy

content.text: SAMS isn't just a database; it's a workflow improver that saves hours of manual work every week.

blogs.title: Enhancing Browser Privacy: The Story Behind MorphAgent
blogs.excerpt: Take control of your digital fingerprint. MorphAgent allows you to instantly spoof your user agent and touch points.

content.text: Privacy on the web is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain. Browser fingerprinting is a common technique used to track users across sites. MorphAgent was born out of the need for a simple, effective tool to counter this.
What is MorphAgent?
MorphAgent is a Firefox extension that lets you spoof your User Agent string and touch capability settings. This makes your browser appear as a different device or browser to websites.
Under the Hood

items: **70+ Profiles**: Choose from a wide range of device and browser profiles
**Per-Site Rules**: Customize settings for specific websites
**Privacy Focused**: Runs locally with no data collection

content.text: Privacy shouldn't be complicated. MorphAgent puts control back in the user's hands with a single click.

Building a browser extension comes with its own set of challenges, particularly around ensuring compatibility and performance without breaking web pages. MorphAgent addresses this by being lightweight and user-configurable.

content.caption: MorphAgent's clean interface for selecting user agent profiles.

blogs.title: Why Rust is Perfect for Network Monitoring Tools
blogs.excerpt: Exploring the development of RustPing, a high-performance network monitoring tool inspired by PRTG.

content.text: When it comes to network monitoring, speed and reliability are non-negotiable. That's why I chose Rust to build RustPing, a modern alternative to traditional monitoring tools.
Why Rust?

Rust's memory safety guarantees and zero-cost abstractions make it an ideal choice for system-level programming. It allows RustPing to handle high-throughput network tasks with minimal resource usage.
RustPing Features

items: **Real-time Monitoring**: Track network health with live updates
**Low Latency**: Optimized for speed and efficiency
**Modern UI**: Built with React and Vite for a smooth user experience

content.text: Rust allows us to write code that is both safe and incredibly fast, a perfect combination for network tools.
Combining a Rust backend with a modern React frontend provides the best of both worlds: raw performance where it counts and a responsive, interactive interface for the user.

content.caption: Monitoring network status in real-time with RustPing.

blogs.title: Building GitHub Burner: Turning Repository Data into an AI-Powered Developer Roast
blogs.excerpt: How GitHub Burner combines live profile analysis, Gemini-generated commentary, exports, and social sharing in one developer-focused experience.

content.text: GitHub profiles contain more than repository names. Languages, activity, project descriptions, and public statistics together reveal patterns in how a developer works. GitHub Burner turns those signals into a playful, personalized roast instead of presenting another conventional analytics dashboard.
From Profile URL to Personalized Output

The application fetches repositories, language usage, profile statistics, and coding patterns from GitHub. That structured context is then passed to Gemini to generate commentary based on the developer's actual public work rather than a generic template.
Product Features

items: Deep analysis of repositories, languages, and public profile statistics
Gemini-powered roasts grounded in the collected GitHub context
Dark and light themes with focused micro-interactions
One-click sharing for professional and social platforms
PDF and JSON export options
Optional user-provided API keys to manage rate limits

content.text: Architecture and Deployment

GitHub Burner uses a Vite-powered React and TypeScript frontend with an Express service layer. Production deployments keep primary API credentials in hosting secrets, while local users can supply a Gemini key through the interface when they want direct control.
The interesting engineering problem was not generating a joke—it was collecting enough relevant context to make the result feel specific to one developer.

blogs.title: Designing Rust-Crypt with AES-256-GCM and Argon2
blogs.excerpt: A look at the authenticated-encryption pipeline, password-based key derivation, portable file format, and CLI design behind Rust-Crypt.

content.text: Rust-Crypt is a cross-platform command-line utility for encrypting and decrypting files with a password. The goal was to keep the workflow approachable while using modern cryptographic building blocks and a file format that contains everything required for safe decryption except the password.
The Encryption Pipeline

items: Generate a unique random salt for every encrypted file
Derive a 256-bit encryption key from the password with Argon2
Generate a random 12-byte nonce
Encrypt and authenticate the file with AES-256-GCM
Store the salt length, salt, nonce, and encrypted payload in a portable binary format

content.text: Why Authenticated Encryption Matters

AES-GCM does more than conceal file contents. Its authentication tag also allows the application to detect corrupted or modified ciphertext instead of returning silently altered data. Argon2 makes password guessing more expensive by applying a dedicated password-based key derivation process.
A Small, Portable CLI

Clap provides clear encrypt and decrypt commands, while anyhow keeps error propagation readable. The resulting binary works across Windows, macOS, and Linux and can be compiled with Cargo in release mode.
A security tool should make the safe path understandable: one password, authenticated encryption, explicit commands, and errors that fail clearly.

content.caption: Rust-Crypt packages salt, nonce, and authenticated ciphertext into a portable encrypted file.

blogs.title: Building GuestIT Portal for Faster Hospitality Support
blogs.excerpt: How a React and Supabase portal connects hotel guests with IT teams through real-time requests, dashboards, authentication, and reporting.

content.text: Technology issues in a hotel room directly affect the guest experience, but Wi-Fi, smart TV, and digital-service complaints often travel through several departments before reaching IT. GuestIT Portal creates a direct workflow for submitting, tracking, and resolving those requests.
Designing for Guests and IT Teams

The guest-facing experience prioritizes a responsive request flow that works comfortably on phones and tablets. The staff side adds authenticated access, current request data, dashboard summaries, and reporting tools so the IT team can manage work from one interface.
Core Capabilities

items: Supabase authentication for protected staff workflows
Real-time request synchronization across active sessions
Dashboards with operational metrics and summaries
PDF reporting for request and guest records
Browser notifications for newly submitted assistance requests
Responsive light and dark themes built with Shadcn UI

content.text: A Typed Full-Stack Workflow

React and TypeScript power the interface, while Supabase provides PostgreSQL, authentication, and real-time data. TanStack Query manages server state, React Hook Form handles form workflows, and Zod validates input before it reaches the backend.
The value of the portal is operational: fewer handoffs, clearer request ownership, and faster visibility for the team responsible for resolving the issue.

content.caption: GuestIT Portal provides a direct request channel between hotel guests and IT operations.

blogs.title: Building a Privacy-First Invoice Studio in the Browser
blogs.excerpt: Inside Invoicely Studio's account-free architecture, local persistence, customizable templates, payment QR codes, and high-fidelity PDF exports.

content.text: Freelancers and small businesses often need professional invoices without adopting a full accounting platform. Invoicely Studio is designed as a focused workspace that runs entirely in the browser, requires no account, and keeps client and financial data under the user's control.
Privacy as an Architecture Decision

Invoice details, client lists, financial settings, and signatures are not sent to an application server. The project uses browser storage for automatic persistence and provides JSON import and export so users can create their own portable backups.
Features for Real Billing Work

items: Custom invoice themes and brand color palettes
Digital signatures embedded into documents
Payment QR codes for faster settlement
Multiple currencies and configurable GST calculations
Local persistence with JSON backup and restore
Print-ready PDF generation with compact layout options

content.text: Generating Reliable PDFs

The interface is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and targeted vanilla CSS. The PDF workflow uses @react-pdf/renderer to translate invoice state into consistent downloadable documents while keeping the editing experience responsive.
Keeping invoicing data client-side turns privacy from a promise into a property of the product's architecture.

content.caption: Invoicely Studio combines local-first data handling with customizable, print-ready invoices.
